$comment: One sample of every event the server pushes down a visitor's live stream.
Both sides of the wire assert against this file and neither one owns it.
tools/check-visitor-events.ts drives the real server code and checks what it
publishes has these shapes; the Dart SDK's fake server replays these samples
rather than literals somebody typed. A key renamed on either side now breaks
It exists because of a bug it would have caught on day one: the Dart client
read 'type' and 'message' while the server sent 'kind' and 'payload', so
every agent reply was dropped before it reached the UI — and the SDK's own
test passed throughout, because its fake server had been written from the
client's expectation instead of the server's contract. Two halves agreeing
with each other and neither with production is the failure this prevents.
Values are illustrative. Only the shape is the contract: which keys exist,
and what kind of thing each holds.

payload.body: Your driver is two minutes away
